body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

violet_c_okline: The violet flame leaps high as your spoken melody rings true, carrying the old vespers of the Nightmother across the cold ash. Soft owl-feather shadows rise in the heat, warming the stone beneath your boots.
violet_c_missline: Your words stumble, and the shrouded dead twist the Nightmother's hymn into a screeching choir of strangled birds inside the fire. Everyone in the lantern ring flinches back from that sour, ringing discord.
violet_dies: The last grain of time runs out, and the violet flame gutters down into cold black grease. Yorgrim reaches a grey hand into his own chest, tearing loose a pale blue spark to keep the ember alive.
violet_spent: I will feed more of my own marrow into the ash so the fire asks fewer words of you next time. My hands look thinner in the lantern light now, but the work remains.
violet_again: The ember still holds its heat, so draw your breath and try the words again without blame.
violet_done: The violet beacon roars up like a furnace, driving the clammy shroud back from the bone-white urns of the Cremation Gardens. Far across the cemetery, a solitary sconce catches fire above the great sepulcher doors.
violet_thanks: Lethica walks under quiet feathers once more, gentle as the dusk she kept. You gave her back her true name before the dark took her.
violet_all_lit: Five fires burn against the gray, and my own blue lantern grows light in the chain. The heavy sepulcher doors will unbar for us now, so come back to the center.
amber_scene: You stand before a rusted iron brazier in the sunken mud of the Potter's Field, where crooked wooden markers rot in the wet clay. Isolde holds her hooded lantern steady in her jaws, pressing the grave-mist back a few paces.
amber_facts: Jericho was a scarecrow man with a battered banjo, walking the muddy roads to trade songs for supper. Children followed his dry straw coat through every village, and he listened to their small troubles as hard as he played. He mended broken plows, split kindling, and left every leaning fence straighter than he found it.
amber_nokindle: The dry straw for his fire is tucked under some stone nearby, though the fog has eaten where I laid it. Look again among the markers, nothing is lost yet.
amber_flame: The dry straw catches in the iron bowl, and a warm amber fire climbs with the smell of autumn harvest. Beyond the light, the wet clay churns as restless dead claw free to throw themselves at the blaze.
amber_hold: Keep your boots inside the lantern ring and cut down whatever crawls from the mud. Their husks must fall where the amber fire can see them die.
amber_rite_prompt: The amber flame leans toward your breath, hungry for the honest measure of Ol' Jericho Sticks in the songs he strummed, the tall tales he spun, and the humble work of his straw-stuffed hands.
amber_a_intro: You turn the rite toward the porch-step tunes Jericho plucked on his old gut-string banjo. Each of you searches your memory for a chorus warm enough to beat back the damp.
amber_a_okline: The amber fire surges up with a crackle like dry pine, humming with the steady rhythm of a country reel. For a breath, the sour mud smells of cider and rosin.
amber_a_missline: The cadence breaks on your tongue, and the shrouded spirits in the smoke rasp back a broken, snapping-string mockery of Jericho's tune. You wince as the sour noise scrapes across your teeth.
amber_b_intro: You steer the words toward the cheerful whoppers Jericho told around village hearths to make frightened folk laugh. Each of you reaches for the wildest yarn that still rings true.
amber_b_okline: The flame jumps bright and golden, dancing like grease in a hot skillet as the tall tale lands right. A dry, rustling chuckle seems to pass through the dead weeds at your ankles.
amber_b_missline: The story sours in the telling, and the hungry shapes in the fire twist the yarn into a spiteful lie about rotting harvests and starved children. The cruel hiss of it makes every shoulder round against the cold.
amber_c_intro: You bring the rite home to the calloused work of his hands, mending tools and turning stubborn soil for strangers. Each of you names a quiet kindness left behind in barn or field.
amber_c_okline: The amber blaze swells thick and steady, throwing out the honest heat of a blacksmith's forge and freshly turned earth. The frost on the iron brazier melts away in a hiss of steam.
amber_c_missline: Your words miss the mark, and the shrouded dead curl the smoke into the shape of a broken pitchfork and a burning barn. The bitter stink of charred burlap makes you turn your faces aside.
amber_dies: The minute bleeds away, and the golden flame sinks down into a sullen smudge of black soot. Yorgrim bows his chained shoulders and breaks off another pale splinter of his own spirit to shelter the spark.
amber_spent: Take another piece of my breath to grease the wood, and the fire will not ask so much of your voices. The names carved on my back feel heavier when I fade like this.
amber_again: No fault lies on your tongues, and the spark still waits in the straw whenever you are ready to speak.
amber_done: The amber beacon roars high, rolling the cold fog back from the sunken trenches of the Potter's Field like dry chaff before a broom. Far away through the iron palings, another sconce flares to life above the sepulcher doors.
amber_thanks: Old straw and sweet music, that was the whole of him before the rot set in. He rests easy in the dark now because you remembered.
amber_all_lit: All five beacons answer my blue lantern now, and the weight on my chains is nearly done. The sepulcher doors are unsealed, so walk with me back to the middle.
magenta_scene: You stand between the towering marble vaults of the Mausoleum Lanes, where cold rainwater drips from carved gargoyles into a dark bronze brazier. Isolde's lantern casts long, sharp shadows across the wet flagstones, holding the gray shroud at bay.
magenta_facts: Briggsy Kratch was a cutthroat pirate with a soft heart, who never once left a loyal sailor behind on the gallows. He fought with a fast blade and a faster tongue, smiling through every trap he laid. Luck loved him at cards and dice until he grew greedy and bound fate itself with crooked sorcery.
magenta_nokindle: The salt-tarred wood for his brazier is stashed in one of these stone niches, though my head is too thick with mist to name which. Search the crypts again, the dead have nothing better to do than wait.
magenta_flame: The tarred kindling catches with a hiss of salt spray, sending a fierce magenta flame twisting toward the marble roofs. Out in the lanes, rusted crypt gates shriek open as armored bones march forth to feed the fire.
magenta_hold: Stand fast within the lantern's circle and break the bones that cross the flagstones. Spill them where the magenta fire can drink their shadow.
